answered.question: What does the catalyst matcher require that the collected rows do not supply? (opened 2026-09-13, on IHH's no_identified_catalyst against eight dated rows)
answered.answer: NOTHING. It never sees them. engines/events/catalyst.py:189 scores a list of typed Event objects against the residual; articles are not candidates.
answered.proof: data/facts.db holds 4,007 events and NOT ONE belongs to a Bursa name: 3,922 from fmp, 46 from fred, 32 from edgar, 7 from finnhub. Per-instrument counts are XNAS:AAPL 1,802, XNAS:NVDA 1,161, XNAS:MSFT 998, MACRO:US 46, and nothing else. Every one of those routes is US-only; bursa_announcements answers 403.
answered.consequence: For the six Malaysian names the candidate list is empty before any evidence is weighed, so no_identified_catalyst is structurally the only verdict a significant Bursa move can receive - however good the evidence is. Tenaga drew it on a session that collected a q1.00 bodied row naming the company and describing what it did.

lessons: A verdict that says 'nothing matched' should not be readable as 'nothing was there to match'. no_identified_catalyst on a Bursa name reports an empty candidate list, and the page that quotes it without saying so is reporting a data gap as an analytical finding.
When a component takes a list, check what is in the list before judging what it did with it. Three pages read the catalyst matcher as too strict; it was never given anything to be strict about.
An event's sign is part of its evidence. A dividend increase on a day the name fell 1.64% is not a weak explanation, it is an explanation pointing the wrong way, and saying so costs nothing.
Coverage that names the company is not the same as coverage about the company. Six of Maybank's rows name it as the research house issuing a call on somebody else.

A source that fails is not a source that is gone. Both of this week's outages - nst_business on 404, edgar on 429 - recovered on the next sweep without intervention, and both were written up as worse than they were.
